title: RxStatus
description: The pharmacy's answer to a NewRx (the NCPDP SCRIPT Status, Verify or Error equivalent, as JSON): it accepted the prescription, or rejected it with a reason. Sent by the simulated pharmacy for the demo, later by the e-prescribing vendor's adapter (Q12), to /hooks/erx, whose receiver hands the body to record_status() in the medications service. `sent` is not a reply: the adapter records it when the NewRx is delivered, and `error` when the outbox gives up. It is filed once per prescription: a second reply with the same `correlationId` changes nothing, and neither does any reply after `accepted` or `rejected`. x-phi marks each field's sensitivity as the API contract does (EXTENSIONS.md).

schemaVersion.description: This shape's version. A change that is not backward-compatible gets a new major version.

correlationId.description: The NewRx's `correlationId`: our prescription ID (NCPDP RelatesToMessageID).

responseId.description: The pharmacy's ID for this reply (NCPDP MessageID), kept as the transmission's vendor message ID. Never a patient identifier.

status.description: `accepted` (the pharmacy took the prescription; NCPDP Status 000 or Verify) or `rejected` (it won't fill it; NCPDP Error). Both are final.

rejection.description: Why it was rejected. Required when `status` is `rejected`, absent otherwise.

code.description: NCPDP SCRIPT error code (`900` transaction rejected, `601` receiver unable to process, `602` receiver system error).

descriptionCode.description: NCPDP SCRIPT DescriptionCode, the detail of the error (e.g. `1000`).

message.description: The pharmacy's reason in words, shown to the prescriber as the transmission's message. It may name the drug or the patient, so it is clinical data and never logged.

Timestamp.description: An instant, RFC 3339, UTC with Z.
